title: AUGUR app manifest, contract 3
description: An app's manifest.json under the app contract (ADR 0075, 0076). It declares what the shell can know before the app's code runs: name, icon, places, commands, radial actions, About sections, settings, intents and the scopes the app asks for. Parts and resources are not here: they are in the app's Score files. Rules a schema cannot say are listed in the spec's section 'Registry checks'.

id.description: The app's id. Its route (/<id>), gateway prefix (/api/<id>), sign-in client (app-<id>), schema, bucket and network are named after it. Reserved ids (AUGUR's own parts) are refused by the registry.

contract.description: The one contract major the app speaks (decision 8, option A). It fixes the gateway API, SDK, Quill and resource-type majors the shell and runner serve. Under option B this field is replaced by `majors` (see the spec, section 11).

description.description: One line shown under the app's name.

icon.description: A kit icon name (Lucide, through Common's Icon).

requiredRole.description: Only people with this role can open it.

floors.description: The kinds of floor the app works on; every kind without it.

entry.description: The ES module the shell loads into the app's sandbox, as a path inside the release's frontend artifact. Never an absolute address: the shell serves it.

frontend.description: The app's frontend. Absent for an app with no UI (a backend-only app).

openapi.description: The path on the inbound part where it serves its OpenAPI document (for example openapi.json); the registry reads it after install.

api.description: The API the app's inbound part answers at /api/<id>. Required when a part declares an inbound route.

scopes.description: The AUGUR APIs the app asks to call, as <api>:<verb>. The registry refuses a scope this AUGUR does not offer. An app may always register itself and read its own settings.

maxUpload.description: The largest request body, in MB, the gateway lets through to the app's inbound part; 10 without it. An admin can lower it.

contributes.description: What the shell draws for the app without loading its code (the VS Code split, ADR 0075 point 6).

places.description: The rail's entries for this app (ADR 0075 point 9). An app may fill in what sits under a place at run time, but cannot add places.

detail.description: One short line on what is there.

path.description: Where in the app it opens, below /<id>. Defaults to /<place id>.

role.description: Only for people with this role on the floor.

floors.description: Only on these kinds of floor; the app's floors without it.

fills.description: The app fills what sits under this place at run time (ctx.frame.under).

commands.description: Named things the app can do, for the command palette, the radial menu and keyboard shortcuts. The shell shows them; the app handles them (ctx.frame.onCommand).

when.description: When the shell offers it: always, only with something selected, or only on one of the app's screens.

radial.description: Actions on the radial menu for a kind of thing the app shows. Each names a command.

on.description: The kind of thing, as the app names its remote elements' `kind` property.

about.description: The sections of the About panel (the drawer) the app fills at run time (ctx.frame.about).

settings.description: Settings an admin fills in under Admin → Apps, never in .env (ADR 0075 point 6). Typed; a secret has no default and reaches a part only as a file.

handles.description: Intent types this app handles, such as document.open.

notifications.description: The kinds of notification the app sends (ADR 0036). Needs notifications:send.

inbox.description: The kinds of work the app puts in people's inboxes (ADR 0026). Needs inbox:write.

search.description: The app's inbound part answers GET /v1/search?q= and the shell's Find asks it.

card.description: Home draws a card for the app, which the app fills through ctx.frame.card.

canvas.description: The app uses the full-canvas sandboxed frame for free drawing (ADR 0076). Shown to the admin before install.

frame.description: How the shell lays out the app's pane until a page says otherwise (ctx.frame.set). Every layout is the shell's, drawn from the kit's tokens; an app chooses one, never a distance.

layout.description: focus: one main column, no About panel. aside: the main column and the About panel. split: a list beside its detail. canvas: one column edge to edge. Without it, aside when the app declares About sections and focus when it doesn't.

width.description: The main column's width (PDR-014); read without it.

density.description: The app's default spacing; the person's own setting overrides it. comfortable without it.

inset.description: flush puts the screen against the pane's edges, for a canvas or media; the page head keeps its inset. standard without it.

about.description: Whether the About panel starts open, in a layout that has it. folded without it.

previews.description: Features the app has ready to try before they're everyone's: admins say who gets each, people opt in, and the app asks ctx.previewOn(id).

links.description: The app binds its things to entities and publishes the binding events (ADR 0025, 0066). Stands until the floor graphs specification decides otherwise (ADR 0077 point 7).

bindings.description: With links.entities, the types of thing the app binds, each published on <app>.<type>.entity-bound and -unbound.

id.description: How the app's parts name it: `${resources.settings.<id>}`.

required.description: The app does not start until an admin has filled it in. Only a secret or a string may be required; everything else has a default.
